Irrespective of the final output size, an atom is a simple circle in proportion to its outline thickness, highlight, and shade. In this case, a 20px circle, 2px outline.
The highlight and shade lie at 70% of the atom’s size.
The width of the highlight and shade is 30% of the atom’s diameter.
In most cases, the highlight always is white and its opacity is 40%. Shade is always 20% darker than the atom’s color.
The preferred highlight is from the top-left, hence a 45° rotation of the atoms.
Convert the highlight and shadow stroke to the outline.
While scaling the atom, we have to enable the Scale Corners and disable the Scale Strokes and Effects option.
As we transform the atom size, the stroke value will remain the same i.e 2 px and the shadow and lighting will alter proportionally with the size of an atom.
Note: use 2 px stroke till 200px atom’s size, after 200 increase 1px for every 100px.
